title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a dictionary between finite combinatorial maps ('cartes') on surfaces and finite sets R of flags ('repères'). The flag set carries three involutions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞, which change the vertex, edge and face component of a flag respectively. The products ρ_i are the 'rotations': ρ_1 = τ_0τ_∞ and ρ_0 = τ_1τ_∞ (and ρ_∞ correspondingly). On the previous page the maps were 'special', meaning ρ_1 (alias σ_1) acts without fixed points. Every edge then carries 4 flags. He now drops that restriction by allowing 'folded' (pliée/aplatie) edges. Geometrically such an edge is a half-edge with one end at a marked vertex and the other end at a free endpoint. That endpoint is a topological vertex of valence 1 of the underlying graph K, but it is a type-1 point (edge midpoint) of the barycentric subdivision, not a marked vertex. Along such an edge there are only 2 flags r and r'.

Formula (10): r' = τ_∞ r = τ_0 r. Equivalently τ_0τ_∞ r = r, i.e. ρ_1 r = r. So folded edges correspond bijectively to: (i) type-1 vertices of the barycentric subdivision that are endpoints (valence 1) of K; (ii) fixed points of ρ_1 = τ_0τ_∞ acting on R.

He contrasts this with a genuine univalent marked vertex (type 0) at the end of an ordinary edge. There the edge still has 4 distinct flags. For each of the two flags at the univalent end, τ_1 and τ_∞ agree (only one edge and only one face-side locally). This gives (11): τ_1 r = τ_∞ r, i.e. ρ_0 r = r. Univalent vertices are therefore in bijection with pairs {r, r'} satisfying r' = τ_1 r = τ_∞ r.

The page breaks off with 'la condition (11) n'implique pas que …'. The next page completes this: (11) does not force τ_0 r = τ_1 r = τ_∞ r, which would be the folded case.

Conclusion drawn on the next page: with folded maps, the categorical equivalences no longer need ρ_1 to act freely. Only the freeness of the τ_i remains, which he says will be removed later (boundaries). He then passes to the symmetric version: the free product Π_{03}^τ = Z/2*Z/2*Z/2, with no relation (τ_0τ_∞)^2 = 1, and its index-2 subgroup Π_{03} = free group <ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ | ρ_∞ρ_1ρ_0 = 1>. These amount to hypermaps (non-oriented and oriented) and dessins d'enfants / π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}).

The problem served is extending the equivalence between finite sets with action of the cartographic group C_2 = <τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞ | τ_i^2 = (τ_0τ_∞)^2 = 1> and maps (and then Belyi covers) to arbitrary actions, without freeness hypotheses.
errors: The phrase 'Pour un pt. bord de K qui est un sommet [marqué/unique] de K (i.e. un sommet de type 1 de la subdivision barycentrique)' is problematic. As the subsequent analysis via (11) and ρ_0 shows, the univalent marked vertex is of type 0, not type 1. Either the transcription or Grothendieck's parenthesis is a slip; the mathematics that follows treats it as a type-0 vertex.

The relations themselves are consistent. If ρ_1 = τ_0τ_∞ and ρ_0 = τ_1τ_∞, then (10) and (11) are correct readings of the local flag pictures. The labels inside the second figure (e.g. 'τ_0τ_∞ = τ_1ρ r') are hard to read and should not be relied on.

ideas.what: Folded edges (half-edges ending at a free end) as fixed points of the edge rotation ρ_1 = τ_0τ_∞ on flags; removing the freeness of σ_1 in the map/permutation dictionary
ideas.modern_name: free edges / semi-edges / dangling half-edges in maps; fixed points of σ_1 in the permutation description of maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones & Singerman, 'Theory of maps on orientable surfaces' (1978), which already allows free edges; Bryant & Singerman (1985) for maps with boundary
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2-3, discusses the cartographic groups C_2 and C_2^+ and removing freeness hypotheses, but not this folded-edge picture in detail

ideas.what: Univalent vertices characterized by τ_1 r = τ_∞ r, i.e. fixed points of ρ_0 on flags (pairs of flags)
ideas.modern_name: valence-1 vertices = fixed points / 1-cycles of the vertex rotation σ_0

ideas.what: Passing from C_2 to the free product Z/2*Z/2*Z/2 and its index-2 free subgroup of rank 2 (next page), to symmetrize the roles of 0, 1, ∞
ideas.modern_name: hypermaps (Walsh/Cori), extended triangle group Δ(∞,∞,∞), cartographic group of dessins
ideas.usually_credited_to: Walsh (1975), Cori (1975), Jones & Singerman; Grothendieck's Esquisse for dessins
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of dessins d'enfants and π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine local analysis of flags at folded edges and univalent vertices. It extends the map/permutation dictionary to non-free ρ_1, which matches the free edges already handled by Jones–Singerman (1978) and the boundary maps of Bryant–Singerman. It is of historical interest as a working draft behind the Esquisse's cartographic-group remarks, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Second line of (10): the image reads 'i.e. τ_0τ_∞ r = r i.e. ρ_1 r = r', consistent with the transcription; the stray symbol after 'τ_0 r' in the first line is a scribble.
'opérant sur R' at the end of the first paragraph: the symbol looks like a script R (the flag set), not a question mark.
'sommet unique de K' is likely 'sommet marqué de K'; the parenthesis 'type 1' may well be 'type 0' in intent.
'sommet le univalent' / 'sommets univalents' are plausible readings ('unisigné' is less likely); the struck word is 'sommet'.
'(ils sont[?] en corr. biunivoque ...)' – reading 'ils sont en corr. biunivoque avec les paires de repères {r,r'}' fits the image.
